subject: alacritty_terminal 0.26 + a TD-owned read loop; TD writes Kitty graphics itself
field_means: who owns the read and parse loop, whether it is thread-safe, and whether it includes a PTY layer
value: By default the library owns the loop: EventLoop::spawn starts a "PTY reader" thread that owns the PTY, takes a lease plus an unfair lock on Arc<FairMutex<Term>> and calls Processor::advance on up to 1 MiB at a time. It includes a PTY layer (tty::Pty over rustix-openpty; ConPTY on Windows). Under this option the embedder owns the loop: Term is a plain struct with no internal locking, Processor::advance(&mut term, bytes) is public, and TD must flush a pending synchronized update (Processor::stop_sync / sync_bytes_count, both public) before acting on a graphics command.
remark: [measured] thread name at event_loop.rs:206, lease at :117 and unfair lock at :140-142, READ_BUFFER_SIZE 0x10_0000 at :24; stop_sync / sync_bytes_count at vte ansi.rs:315,362.

subject: alacritty_terminal 0.26 + a TD-owned read loop; TD writes Kitty graphics itself
field_means: how its answers to programs' queries reach the embedding program
value: Replies are events, not writes: Term calls EventListener::send_event(Event::PtyWrite(String)) for DA, DSR and mode reports, and TextAreaSizeRequest / ColorRequest / ClipboardLoad carry formatter closures. Nothing in the library writes them to the PTY; the embedder does, which is how TD answers exactly once in the host (host.rs:744) while the window replica swallows PtyWrite and TextAreaSizeRequest (term.rs:95-101). Kitty a=q replies would be written by TD's own loop, since vte never sees the query.

subject: rio-vt — Rio's embeddable core (crates.io)
field_means: which parts of the Kitty graphics protocol it implements
value: Broad, inside the crate. Transmission: t=d with chunking, t=f, t=t (path must contain tty-graphics-protocol; deleted after reading), t=s (shm_open on Unix, a file mapping on Windows). Formats: f=8, f=16, f=24, f=32 raw and f=100 PNG; PNG decodes only with the non-default `graphics` feature, otherwise EINVAL. o=z zlib with a decompressed-size cap. Placement: a=T and a=p at the cursor with x/y/w/h source rectangle, c/r cell span, X/Y sub-cell offset, C=1, z index. U=1 virtual placements are stored as metadata and ansi/kitty_virtual.rs supplies the placeholder decoders, but scanning cells for U+10EEEE and compositing is the embedder's renderer's job. Deletes: a/A, i/I, n/N, c/C, p/P, x/X, y/Y, z/Z, q/Q, r/R. a=q runs the real load path and answers OK or the error, honouring q=. Limits: 320 MiB image store per terminal with eviction of unreferenced images; 10000 px per axis and 400 MiB payload at parse; 4096x4096 display cap. Not implemented: animation (a=f, a=a, a=c answered EINVAL:unsupported action) and relative placements (P/Q/H/V parsed, never used).

subject: rio-vt — Rio's embeddable core (crates.io)
field_means: who owns the read and parse loop, whether it is thread-safe, and whether it includes a PTY layer
value: The embedder chooses. Headless, the embedder owns the loop and calls Processor::advance(&mut term, bytes) on a Crosswords it holds, with no threads. With the default `pty` feature, performer::Machine spawns a 'PTY reader' thread that polls a teletypewriter PTY through corcovado and parses into an Arc<FairMutex<Crosswords<U>>> shared with the renderer (U: EventListener + Send + 'static). Crosswords has no internal locking. The PTY layer (teletypewriter) is included and can be dropped with default-features = false. Synchronized updates: an embedder loop should poll Processor::sync_timeout(); otherwise advance() flushes an expired update when the next bytes arrive.

Create a grid, feed it bytes through the parser, and read cells back. No
PTY, no renderer, no threads:

subject: rio-vt — Rio's embeddable core (crates.io)
field_means: how its answers to programs' queries reach the embedding program
value: An event callback. Replies (DA1/DA2, DSR/CPR, DECRQM, XTGETTCAP, Kitty acks and a=q answers) are sent as RioEvent::PtyWrite(route_id, String) through EventListener::send_event. Window-size reports arrive as TextAreaSizeRequest, OSC colour queries as ColorRequest and OSC 52 reads as ClipboardLoad, each carrying a formatter closure the embedder applies before writing. The embedder does the PTY write, so a TD replica can drop these events and let the host answer once — the same shape as alacritty's Event.

subject: libghostty-vt — Ghostty's core as a library, via Rust bindings
field_means: which parts of the Kitty graphics protocol it implements
value: Full core implementation behind the C API (build feature kitty_graphics, on by default). Actions q, t, T, p, d, f, a, c. Media: direct, file, temporary file, shared memory (file/temp/shm are opt-in per terminal; temp is restricted to a directory the embedder names). Formats: RGB (24), RGBA (32), PNG (100) — PNG only if the embedder installs a decode callback, otherwise rejected. zlib compression (o=z), inflated before storage. Placements: direct (anchored to tracked page-list pins), virtual (U=1) and relative (P/Q parent chains). Deletes a, i, n, c, f, p, q, r, x, y, z with upper-case freeing variants. Query and transmit replies go out through the WRITE_PTY callback. z-index with BELOW_BG / BELOW_TEXT / ABOVE_TEXT iterator filters. Animation frames (a=f, a=a, a=c) composed eagerly into RGBA; the current frame is exposed, but timed playback is driven by the Ghostty app renderer (ImageStorage.animationTick) and has no C API entry point, so an embedder sees client-driven frame changes only. Storage quota per screen (0 disables) and a 65 MiB APC buffer cap. Read side: GhosttyKittyGraphics handle, placement iterator with layer filter, image lookup returning decoded pixels plus generation stamps, and render_info geometry. Unicode placeholders: the API reports is_virtual and a per-row KITTY_VIRTUAL_PLACEHOLDER flag, but position/rect calls return NO_VALUE for virtual placements, so the embedder must decode U+10EEEE cells (diacritics, fg-colour image id) itself.

(2) VT formatter: ghostty_formatter_terminal_new with GHOSTTY_FORMATTER_FORMAT_VT re-encodes the screen as VT bytes with optional extras (cursor, SGR, OSC 8, protection, kitty keyboard, charsets, palette, modes, scrolling region, tabstops, pwd) — the route zmx takes through the Zig API. Neither route carries Kitty image or placement state.
quote: A snapshot is an ordered, CRC-protected record stream. Its READY marker follows enough state to render and resume the terminal, including any unfinished VT parser input. Older scrollback pages follow READY and the FINISH marker terminates the complete snapshot.

subject: libghostty-vt — Ghostty's core as a library, via Rust bindings
field_means: who owns the read and parse loop, whether it is thread-safe, and whether it includes a PTY layer
value: The embedder owns the read loop: libghostty-vt has no PTY layer, no event loop, no timer and no background thread; bytes go in through ghostty_terminal_vt_write, and every effect callback runs synchronously on the calling thread (no re-entrant vt_write). The C API has no internal locking; the render docs expect a lock held across render-state update. The Rust bindings make every type !Send and !Sync, so a terminal lives on one thread and talks through channels.
quote: In particular, all libghostty-vt types are !Send, meaning they cannot be transferred across threads, since the C API is allowed to use thread-local state; they are also !Sync, meaning they cannot be shared across threads, since data races may occur as the C API is not guarded with mutexes or other synchronization mechanisms.
remark: [measured] docs.rs Thread safety section (line breaks collapsed). No timer/thread: terminal docs "libghostty-vt does not create a timer or background thread."; callbacks: "All callbacks are invoked synchronously during VT writes."; lock guidance render.h:29-34.

subject: libghostty-vt — Ghostty's core as a library, via Rust bindings
field_means: how its answers to programs' queries reach the embedding program
value: A per-terminal WRITE_PTY callback receives every reply byte string (DSR, DECRQM, mode 2048 size reports, Kitty graphics a=q and transmit responses). DA1/DA2/DA3, XTWINOPS size, XTVERSION, ENQ and colour-scheme queries are answered by embedder callbacks that return data for the terminal to encode. With no WRITE_PTY installed, reply-producing sequences are silently dropped — so a window replica that installs none, next to a host that installs one, gives exactly-once replies by construction.
quote: Feeds raw bytes through the terminal's VT stream parser, updating terminal state accordingly. By default, sequences that require output (queries, device status reports) are silently ignored. Use ghostty_terminal_set() with GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_WRITE_PTY to install a callback that receives response data.

subject: Contour's vtbackend (C++)
field_means: which parts of the Kitty graphics protocol it implements
value: Partial, shipped in 0.7.0: graphics/KittyGraphics.{hpp,cpp} parse, screen/Screen.cpp (processAPC, processKittyGraphics) executes. Transmit: direct (t=d) only; t=f, t=t and t=s parse but are answered 'ENOTSUP:only direct transmission is supported'. Formats: f=24, f=32, f=100 (PNG). Compression o=z parses but is answered 'ENOTSUP:compressed payloads are not supported'. Chunked m=1, capped at 32 MiB. a=t/a=T store and display; a=p places a stored image at the cursor with c=/r= cell sizing and C=1. Deletes: d=i/I by id (lower case keeps the data, upper case frees it) and d=a/A; every other target, positional and n/N/r/R included, clears all placements. a=q validates exactly as a transmit would and replies OK or the error. z<0 draws on a Below layer, otherwise Above (two layers). a=f/a/c answered 'ENOTSUP:animation not supported'. No U=1 virtual placements (the U key is ignored as unknown). Stored-image quota 128 MiB, ENOSPC on overflow.
quote: Adds the kitty graphics protocol (APC G): transmitting, displaying, placing and deleting images, in PNG or raw RGB/RGBA, including chunked transmission

field_means: who owns the read and parse loop, whether it is thread-safe, and whether it includes a PTY layer
value: The library parses under its own lock; the embedder owns the thread. Terminal holds a plain std::mutex (_stateMutex); Terminal::processInputOnce() reads from its vtpty::Pty and parses under that lock, called in a loop by the embedder's thread (the GUI's TerminalSession::mainLoop, the daemon's per-session blocking-read pump); writeToScreen(string_view) parses bytes from elsewhere. It includes a PTY layer (vtpty: UnixPty, ConPty, SshSession, MockPty, MockViewPty), and the Terminal constructor takes std::unique_ptr<vtpty::Pty>. Events callbacks fire on the parser thread with the mutex held.

subject: Hybrid: alacritty for text, libghostty-vt beside it for pictures only
field_means: whether the whole terminal state can be serialised or replayed for a client that attaches later
value: No, not for pictures. TD's gridwire::encode_snapshot re-encodes only alacritty's grid as VT bytes. libghostty-vt's own binary snapshot (C API added upstream on 2026-08-03, after crate 0.2.1's pin) says Kitty image and placement state is not part of it. So a re-attaching window would get text and no pictures unless TD ships image bytes and placements itself. The window's replica also cannot re-parse t=t or t=s transmissions, because the protocol makes the first terminal that reads them, the host's shadow, delete the file or unlink the shared memory.
quote: // Kitty image and placement state is not part of this snapshot // version, but the placeholder is still a valid Unicode scalar.
remark: [measured] libghostty's snapshot encoder on main. The deletion rule is in the kitty protocol doc (https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/blob/42d3cb2148acc182946901091dbbb0431a5a3344/docs/graphics-protocol.rst#L332-L344): "A temporary file, the terminal emulator will delete the file after reading the pixel data" and, for shared memory, "The terminal emulator must read the data from the memory object and then unlink and close it on POSIX". gridwire.rs (TD) documents a text-only snapshot.

subject: Hybrid: alacritty for text, libghostty-vt beside it for pictures only
field_means: who owns the read and parse loop, whether it is thread-safe, and whether it includes a PTY layer
value: The loop is split. alacritty's EventLoop owns the PTY reader thread and parser, and TD's host.rs TeeReader already copies every read on that thread while holding the lease. libghostty-vt owns no loop, thread or PTY: the embedder calls vt_write. Its Rust handles are !Send + !Sync, so the shadow Terminal must live on one thread. It can be created lazily on alacritty's reader thread (e.g. thread-local per pane) and fed inside TeeReader::read before alacritty parses the chunk. The alternative is a dedicated thread fed through a channel, which loses the ordering that both the attach fence and the a=q reply depend on.
quote: Handle types (`Terminal`, `RenderState`, `KeyEncoder`, etc.) are `!Send + !Sync` by design. Callers should drive all operations from a single thread.
remark: [measured] the crate README. TD's host.rs (terminal-delight@426f072:app/src/host.rs:131-132) says "The copy happens *inside* the read, on the reader thread, while the lease is held — which is what makes the attach fence work." Where the shadow should live is my inference.

subject: Hybrid: alacritty for text, libghostty-vt beside it for pictures only
field_means: how its answers to programs' queries reach the embedding program
value: There are two reply channels, and TD must merge them by hand. alacritty emits Event::PtyWrite(String), which TD bounces to the PTY. libghostty-vt calls its write_pty callback (Rust: Terminal::on_pty_write) for every reply it generates, DA and DSR included. To keep 'exactly once', TD must drop every libghostty reply except Kitty APC responses (ESC _ G ...). Ordering matters as well. kitty's detection recipe is a=q followed by DA1, and a terminal that answers DA1 first is judged to lack pictures. So the shadow must parse each chunk, and write its a=q answer, before alacritty answers a DA1 in the same chunk; viu and kitten icat both send a=q and then CSI c in the captures.
quote: To check if a terminal emulator supports the graphics protocol the best way is to send the above *query action* followed by a request for the `primary device attributes <https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DA1.html>`_. If you get back an answer for the device attributes without getting back an answer for the *query action* the terminal emulator does not support the graphics protocol.
remark: [measured] the protocol doc. libghostty-vt 0.2.1 src/terminal.rs L1534-1536: "Call the given function when the terminal needs to write data back to the pty (e.g. in response to a DECRQM query or device status report)." alacritty_terminal-0.26.0 src/event.rs L39-40: "/// Write some text to the PTY. PtyWrite(String),". Capture: terminal-delight@45567b7:docs/plans/program-pixels/evidence/stand-in/viu-kitty.json events (a=q, reply, then q DA1).

field_means: which parts of the Kitty graphics protocol it implements
value: Yes, since v0.45.0 (PR #5428 'Support the Kitty Image Protocol', merged 2026-07-31). Zellij terminates the protocol in the server and re-emits pictures to each client's host terminal. Because vte 0.15 drops APC, a byte-level KittyApcInterceptor runs ahead of vte in TerminalPane::handle_pty_bytes and captures ESC _ G … ESC \ (1 MiB cap per escape). kitty_graphics/parser.rs: actions a=t, a=T, a=p, a=d, a=q; media t=d, t=f, t=t (temp files under /tmp, /dev/shm or named tty-graphics-protocol are deleted); t=s answered ENOTSUPPORTED; formats f=24, f=32, f=100 (PNG decoded to RGBA); o=z zlib; m=0/1 chunking; x/y/w/h source rect, c/r scaling, X/Y cell offsets, z index, C=1; U=1 virtual placements and a=f/a/c animation answered ENOTSUPPORTED. grid_state.rs delete handles d=a/A, i/I, n/N, c/C, p/P, q/Q, x/X, y/Y, z/Z, r/R. replies.rs writes OK or error replies honouring q=; a=q answers OK only when the client's host terminal supports graphics. store.rs keeps a 320 MiB LRU store. A direct placement without C=1 advances Zellij's cursor (grid.rs advance_cursor_after_kitty_placement). output/mod.rs re-transmits each image once per client (a=t, f=32) and places it with a=p … C=1, deleting stale host placements.

field_means: whether the whole terminal state can be serialised or replayed for a client that attaches later

subject: Zellij — a Rust multiplexer whose server owns its own grid (host/client prior art)
field_means: how its answers to programs' queries reach the embedding program

subject: zmx — server-side snapshots with libghostty-vt (host/replica prior art)
field_means: who owns the read and parse loop, whether it is thread-safe, and whether it includes a PTY layer
value: zmx owns the whole loop: one double-forked daemon process per session, holding the PTY it created with forkpty(); a single-threaded poll(2) loop over the server socket, the PTY master, a signal pipe and each client socket; every PTY read (up to 4096 bytes) is fed to the libghostty-vt stream and broadcast to clients in the same iteration, so there are no threads, no locks and no snapshot/stream seam to fence. Clients are also single-threaded poll(2) loops that pipe stdin to the socket and Output to stdout.
quote:
- The `daemon` and client processes communicate via a unix socket
- Both `daemon` and `client` loops leverage `poll(2)`
- Each session creates its own unix socket file
- We restore terminal state and output using `libghostty-vt`
remark: [measured] Daemon-per-session: loop.zig L565-572; daemonLoop poll: loop.zig L226-292; PTY: daemonize.zig L84 'spawnPty runs forkpty()'; client loop: loop.zig L16-18. Seam absence inferred from the single-threaded structure.

subject: zmx — server-side snapshots with libghostty-vt (host/replica prior art)
field_means: how its answers to programs' queries reach the embedding program
value: Two regimes. With no terminal client attached, zmx itself scans PTY output for DA1/DA2 queries and queues fixed answers (ESC[?62;22c, ESC[>1;10;0c) into the PTY write buffer; nothing else is answered, because the server's libghostty-vt stream is readonly and ignores queries (Kitty a=q, DSR, XTVERSION go unanswered). With clients attached, queries reach every client's own terminal raw, and only the leader client's input — which carries its terminal's replies — is forwarded to the PTY; a non-leader's input is dropped unless it looks like typing (which makes it leader), so each reply is written once.
remark: [measured] Answers: util.zig L257-262 and L264-295. Readonly stream: ghostty Terminal.zig L370 'Sequences that query or otherwise require output will be ignored.' Leader rule: loop.zig L898-908 (handleInput) and isUserInput (util.zig L688-727), which returns true only for printable text, CR/LF/TAB/BS, CSI u/~ and modified arrows. Snapshot is only sent on re-attach 'to avoid interfering with shell initialization (DA1 queries, etc.)' (loop.zig L977-978).
